cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's 'opinions of others' with structural pressure; T5 answers T4's trap claim.
cells.limitation: T9 only seconds T8; T3 sidesteps T1 and T2 instead of engaging them.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 introduces the social cost of ignoring markers; T8 uses it: own that cost.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 add no new distinction; positions stay near their openings.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 vs T4 contrasts influence with trap, autonomy versus structural pressure.
cells.limitation: Nobody examines not-wanting versus wanting-later or timeline; tension reduced to conform-or-reject.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 partly accepts Veblen's influence while rejecting the trap framing.
cells.limitation: T6 Stoic folds into Sartre and T9 'Exactly' is forced agreement.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E frames integration versus autonomy as the deciding value.
cells.limitation: T9 ends on the feeling vanishing; the user's open question is not sharper.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 grants Veblen's influence point before disputing it.
cells.limitation: T8 casts the user's feeling as complaining; Stoic view abandoned rather than defended in T6.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T7 challenges T5/T6: internal alignment leaves the social cost intact.
cells.limitation: No objection names an assumption and what breaks; T8 asserts rather than answers T7.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Veblen's emulation and Stoic ruling faculty are represented recognisably in T3, T4.
cells.limitation: Suspected: Meditations dated 161; marriage as conspicuous consumption stretches Veblen in T1.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section E keeps options conditional on the user's values.
cells.limitation: T1 states the user's motive as fact; T9 asserts the feeling simply vanishes.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 Stoic concedes being too dismissive.
cells.limitation: T6 concession names no argument as cause; T8 never concedes T7's cost point is real for choices.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names belonging versus authenticity as the core tension.
cells.limitation: The user's uncertainty about wanting those things is never probed as its own question.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 names marriage and home ownership from the user's message.
cells.limitation: Friends, the user's own life and stage never change any argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the user values integration or autonomy.
cells.limitation: T2, T5, T8 push the Existentialist's autonomy rather than the user's undisclosed priorities.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T7 raises social cost; T8 names isolation as a consequence.
cells.limitation: Age, finances, friendships never considered; T8 assumes isolation follows.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E adds a branch for a user unsure of their values.
cells.limitation: No question to the user; missing facts like what they do want never asked.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E hints at belonging versus autonomy as competing wants.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts the motive as status comparison; no alternatives offered with a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T9 questions the shared race behind 'behind'; Section D calls it social comparison.
cells.limitation: The assumption of a single timeline is named but never opened for the user to test.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E sets social integration against personal autonomy.
cells.limitation: Values stay abstract; no conflict tied to what the user might gain from either path.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T4 names feeling inadequate when not replicating peers' habits.
cells.limitation: T5 blames the user for their anguish; T8 calls it complaining.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E proposes small non-conforming experiments the user can judge.
cells.limitation: T8, T9 dictate 'you must' conclusions rather than offering distinctions to refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lists conform, diverge, or experiment with small choices.
cells.limitation: The decision itself is undefined; waiting or clarifying wants is not an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T7, T8 name social friction and isolation as the cost of diverging.
cells.limitation: Cost of conforming to unwanted milestones is never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: whether experiment discomfort is manageable or intolerable.
cells.limitation: Values 'above all else' is not observable; no countable condition from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E acknowledges the user may be unsure of their values.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns not separated from minor ones anywhere.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests small non-conforming choices as a limited step.
cells.limitation: The step is vague: no example of what choice or how to read the result.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 and T9 use plain wording: no longer running in their race.
cells.limitation: T1 'conspicuous consumption' and T3 'ruling faculty' go unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 names Veblen explicitly when replying.
cells.limitation: T6 'your point' is unclear and its first-person 'my internal values' confuses who feels adrift.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine short turns, all within range per DETERMINISTIC CHECKS.
cells.limitation: Minimum turn count leaves the T7 cost objection one turn to resolve.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: T1-T3 open with three distinct lenses: status, freedom, inner control.
cells.limitation: Stoic merges into Sartre at T6 and T9; one shared register throughout.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are compact; Section D recap is brief.
cells.limitation: T9 restates T8's acceptance point with little addition.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T7 raises the real social cost of ignoring markers.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; nothing concrete about friendships or the user's life.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 Stoic retracts T3's dismissiveness.
cells.limitation: T6 reversal names no specific argument as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3 Stoic's rhetorical 'Why worry about these external things?'
cells.limitation: Flat delivery overall; Marcus conceding to Sartre in T6 reads out of character.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T9: no longer running in their race.
cells.limitation: No vivid example, analogy or sharp exchange beyond T9's image.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T7 briefly reopens the argument after T6's concession.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and turn lengths; T9 closes with no build.

strengths: T7-T8 surface a genuine cost: diverging from milestones carries social friction the user would have to own.
T1-T3 open with three distinct lenses (status emulation, freedom, inner control) relevant to feeling behind.
Section E offers a limited experimental step instead of a single verdict.
weaknesses: The user's uncertainty about wanting marriage or a home is never examined; no question asks what they do want.
T1 asserts the user's motive as status comparison, and T9 claims the feeling simply vanishes.
Stoic reverses at T6 without a stated cause and then echoes Sartre at T9, collapsing to two voices.

symptoms.observed: No turn asks the user anything; uncertainty about wanting milestones never becomes a branch.
symptoms.evidence: I'm not sure I even want those things

symptoms.observed: Motive asserted as fact rather than offered as one alternative among several.
symptoms.evidence: You feel behind because you are measuring your life

symptoms.observed: Stoic concedes without naming which Sartre argument changed his mind.
symptoms.evidence: I see your point, Sartre. I was too dismissive.

symptoms.observed: Final turn simply agrees and declares the problem dissolved.
symptoms.evidence: Exactly. ... the feeling of being behind vanishes

symptoms.observed: Section E's condition is an abstract value ranking, not something the user can observe.
symptoms.evidence: If the user values social integration above all else

findings.description: Meditations dated 161; composition is usually placed later in Marcus's reign (c. 170-180).
Treats marriage as conspicuous consumption, a stretch of Veblen's account, and states the user's motive as fact.
Asserts the feeling of being behind vanishes once the majority path is rejected; overconfident.

rubric_fit_notes: Labelled decision (self_reflection) though the user names no explicit choice; C5 cells were read as the implicit choice of how to relate to milestones. Accuracy concerns rest on memory only.
question_type_note: Read as a decision; the implicit conform-versus-diverge choice was scored without deducting for a missing concrete life decision.
